## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` infer the correct semver bump (minor vs patch) from the work items being released, instead of always bumping patch, and require an explicit producer-approved justification before a minor bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release contains new user-facing capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), which misrepresents the release's impact and forces the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (agent or operator)** — runs `/skill:ship release` and expects the pipeline to select the semantically correct version part without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must be able to see and approve a minor-version bump with a full justification before it happens, because a minor bump signals new capability to downstream consumers.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a bug fix or chore, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains a new feature, I want the pipeline to detect it and propose a minor bump with the evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to approve or reject a proposed minor bump before any git mutation occurs, with a justification naming the items that triggered it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run-release.js` evaluates the release candidate set (`wl list --stage in_review`) at startup, before the gating checks and the merge, and derives a proposed bump type: `minor` when at least one candidate is minor-worthy, otherwise `patch`.
- The derived decision is logged with the contributing work-item IDs and titles (or an explicit statement that no candidate warrants a minor bump), so the version choice is auditable.
- When the proposed bump is `patch`, the release proceeds with a patch bump automatically — no producer interaction — and the existing `--bump patch` behaviour is unchanged.
- When the proposed bump is `minor`, the release performs no git mutation, prints a full justification (each contributing item ID, title, and why it warrants a minor bump), and exits with a distinct documented exit code until the producer approves the bump (approval mechanism per Appendix Q2).
- An explicit `--bump <patch|minor|major>` always overrides inference, including `major` (major is never inferred).
- A minor bump resets `z` to `0` (e.g. `0.1.19` → `0.2.0`), reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: minor-worthy candidate → minor proposal + approval gate; patch-only candidates → automatic patch; empty candidate set → patch; mixed candidate set → minor; explicit `--bump` override; no git mutation occurs on the approval-pending path; the justification names the correct items.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, the new exit code in the exit-code table, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add new capability will carry a version number that reflects it (minor instead of patch), and producers will see and approve that decision with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (`--bump` validation already rejects anything else).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no inference step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly, including `z = 0` on minor/major bumps, and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are defined as items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set the inferrer must read already exists.
- The release pipeline is non-interactive (agent harness): no TTY prompt facility exists in `run-release.js`.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable classification function (e.g. `deriveBumpFromCandidates(candidates)`) that returns `{ bump: 'minor'|'patch', minorWorthy: [...], reason }` from the release candidate list.
2. Wire the inference into `run-release.js` startup after argument parsing and before the Code Freeze/gating/merge steps; skip inference when `--bump` was supplied explicitly.
3. Patch proposal → pass `--bump patch` through unchanged and log the decision.
4. Minor proposal → print the justification (item IDs, titles, per-item reason) and exit with the new documented code without any git mutation; the producer approves by re-running with `--bump minor` (or the chosen approval flag).
5. Extend the wrapper usage/exit-code table and `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` accordingly.
6. Add unit tests beside the existing ship-skill node tests, following the repo's injectable-boundary style so no test reads or mutates the live worklog.

## Constraints

- **Non-interactive and fail-closed:** the release runs under an agent harness; a minor bump must be blocked (no mutation) until an explicit approval signal is supplied. No blocking TTY prompt.
- **Backward compatible:** explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only decides which bump type to request.
- **No new worklog metadata required:** classification must work from fields the release-candidate query already returns (at minimum `issueType`, `priority`, `stage`). New item tags/labels would be scope creep unless chosen in Appendix Q1.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/malformed candidate list must not silently select minor (default to patch and warn) and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed.
- **Exit-code discipline:** the new code must be distinct from the documented `0`–`14` range and documented in the wrapper usage and exit-code tables.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — argument parsing, startup inference wiring, justification output, new exit code, usage text.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document inference, approval gate, and the new exit code.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — wrapper argument/exit-code reference.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for classification and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Classification ambiguity (risk):** `issueType` is empty on many historical items, and "feature" vs "task" is not always a clean semver signal. Mitigation: conservative default to patch, explicit `--bump` override, and the justification lists every contributing item so the producer can correct the decision. Resolved by Appendix Q1.
- **Approval UX (risk):** the pipeline is non-interactive, so "ask the producer" must become an explicit re-run signal; a wrong choice here either blocks automated releases or silently skips approval. Mitigation: fail-closed exit with a copy-pasteable approval command. Resolved by Appendix Q2.
- **Major-version inference (assumption):** the seed explicitly scopes inference to `y`/`z` only; major bumps remain deliberate `--bump major` actions. Confirm in Appendix Q3.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, or new worklog metadata are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; bump inference still runs unless `--bump` is explicit. If the producer expects `--skip-checks` to disable inference too, that is a correction to record during review.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (classification rule):** How should an item be judged "minor-worthy"?
  - Option A: by `issueType` — `feature` and `epic` → minor; `bug`, `chore`, `task`, `docs` and empty → patch.
  - Option B: by `priority` — `high`/`critical` → minor.
  - Option C: by an explicit label/tag on the item (new metadata).
  - **Recommended:** Option A — it is the closest existing proxy for "new user-facing capability", needs no new metadata, and a wrong guess is overridable by `--bump`.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How should the producer approve a proposed minor bump in a non-interactive pipeline?
  - Option A: fail-closed — exit with a distinct code and a copy-pasteable command, producer re-runs with `--bump minor` (or a dedicated `--confirm-bump minor` flag).
  - Option B: interactive TTY prompt when stdin is a TTY, with Option A as the non-TTY fallback.
  - Option C: automatic minor bump with a warning (no approval gate) — rejected, because the seed requires approval.
  - **Recommended:** Option A — deterministic for agents, leaves no ambiguous prompt, mirrors the existing fail-closed gates, and keeps the justification in the release log.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should the inference ever propose a `major` (x) bump?
  - Option A: no — only minor/patch are inferred; major stays an explicit `--bump major` action.
  - Option B: yes — infer major for breaking changes (requires a new signalling convention).
  - **Recommended:** Option A — matches the seed description and avoids inventing a breaking-change convention.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** – Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs (completed)
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** – bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, access, action (+344 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, action, actual (+337 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: able, acceptance, accordingly, action, actions (+330 more)

# Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** (residual post-fix slot-wait re-measurement follow-up).

## Problem statement

The `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` harness's genuine-run filter admits tool results from non-bash tools (e.g. `read`) when their text contains structural markers, so fixture text echoed by a file read is parsed as genuine slot-wait measurements — producing a spurious 999.0 s sample that fails the `no_run_over_120s` threshold.

## Target outcome

Fix the `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` false positive so that reading a fixture/source file can never be counted as a genuine test-slot run, restoring a trustworthy `no_run_over_120s` verdict.

## Users

- **Producer / agent operators** running the slot-wait re-measurement harness to verify the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix removed test-slot starvation. A false-positive breach invalidates their verdict and blocks RCA closure.
- Example user story: *As a producer closing the slot-starvation RCA (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV), I need the harness verdict to reflect only real runs, so that a `fail` genuinely means users are still waiting > 120 s for a slot.*

## Existing state (evidence, 2026-11-10)

Running `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window reports a spurious **999.0 s** `dev_push_gate` sample. It is an artefact, not a run:

- An agent `read` `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (session record `2026-11-10T15:23:02.987Z`).
- That file contains the fixture text `"slot_wait_seconds": 999.0` plus a `run_tests: gate-subject` marker.
- The harness's genuine-run filter trusts a tool result whose text carries a structural marker when no bash command is resolvable. A `read` tool result has no bash command, so the fixture text is parsed as **four fake gate samples** (122.687, 9.0, 1.25, 999.0).
- Effect: `dev_push_gate` inflates from 5 calls / max 0.002 s to 9 calls / max 999.0 s, and `no_run_over_120s` fails on a non-existent run.

Reproduction (confirmed): `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import measure_slot_wait as m; print(m.parse_block(open('tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py').read())['gate'])"` — prints the four injected samples.

Root cause: `measure()` pairs each `toolResult` with its assistant `toolCall` command via `_commands_by_tool_call`, which maps **only `bash` tool calls**. A `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep` result therefore resolves to `command=None` and falls through to the `_has_structural_marker` fallback intended for genuine bash runs whose call record is missing (forked/compacted logs).

## Desired change

Distinguish "no command resolvable because the log is incomplete" from "no command because the result came from a non-bash tool". The `toolResult` message itself carries `toolName`; only `bash` results (or a result with no tool name) may use the structural-marker fallback. A result whose `toolName` is a non-bash tool is never a measurement, regardless of its text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `read` (or any non-bash tool) result that merely echoes fixture text is never counted as a genuine run sample.
2. A regression test proves reading `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (and a generic fixture file) injects zero samples.
3. The genuine-run filter still accepts real run sources (`run_tests.py`, `implement.py`, `git push`, `wait_for_job.py`) and genuine structural-marker results with no resolvable command.
4. `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window no longer reports the 999.0 s sample.
5. Testing/validation criterion: the regression test fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The slot-wait re-measurement harness stops reporting phantom breaches, so the parent RCA's threshold verdict is trustworthy.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement tooling; never synthesise load.
- No change to the lane ceilings or threshold values.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — genuine-run filter in `measure()`; also the module docstring's "Attribution — genuine run filter" section.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — regression test for the fixture-echo false positive.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — "Genuine-run filter" paragraph (needs the bash-only rule stated).

## Related work

- `SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU` — the follow-up item whose re-measurement surfaced this artefact.
- `SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K` — the harness's originating item.
- `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` — parent; its AC3 threshold check is the consumer of this verdict.
- `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI` — ruff ISC004 flagging `measure_slot_wait.py`; same file, unrelated lint false-positive, do not conflate with this fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix must not tighten acceptance for valid cases — genuine structural-marker results from bash runs with missing call records must still pass.
- **Confirmed assumption**: `toolResult` messages carry a `toolName` field set to `"bash"` on genuine bash tool results. Verified across a ~3,000-result sample of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: `bash` 2346, `read` 394, `edit` 251, `write` 56, `grep` 17, `skill_path` 1 — every genuine run source is `bash`, so a `toolName != "bash"` guard is safe.
- **Assumption**: no non-bash tool legitimately carries slot-wait data in its result text.
- **Scope-creep risk**: do not extend the fix to other measurement harnesses (`measure_audit_performance.py`) unless they exhibit the same pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the work item description provides sufficient evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria to proceed. Verified independently: (a) the reproduction prints the four injected gate samples; (b) `toolName` is present and `bash`-only for genuine runs across the session corpus; (c) the "Genuine-run filter" docs paragraph is the only prose describing the fallback.
data.title: Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

# Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (
  `--project unit` / `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound,
  the elapsed wall time, the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the
  core count — so contention is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound, i.e. ~1.4× headroom) **plus load-aware scaling** of the
  bound from the sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**;
  the bound remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`).
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline are recorded in the runner/CI header
  comment(s) and in the release-gate documentation (this repo's `docs/`, and TCE's
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header + `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout).
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout (TCE `.pi/test-config.json` →
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, for an 18–21 min suite — ~4–7 min headroom), so raising/scaling an
  inner bound either adjusts the outer budget in the same change or documents why it still fits.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average is injected through a test seam and is
  never read from the real host.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average in a test; sample it behind an
  injectable seam.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- This repo (framework): `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (outer per-command timeout budgeting,
  any stage-bound surface), `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` (gate log surface),
  release-gate docs in `docs/`.
- Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here): `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (hang diagnostic
  content, load-average sampling seam, hybrid bound derivation), `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  (unit-stage `--timeout-ms 300000`, header comment rationale),
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (diagnostic + bound coverage with injected load),
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (hang-timeout section ~line 1313, test-config section ~line 816),
  `.pi/test-config.json` (`timeoutPerCommand: 1500` if the outer budget is adjusted).

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** (TCE, completed) — the project-coverage gate whose fail-closed behaviour
  must be preserved.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this
  brief; measured evidence and the evidence corrections (retry log shows a producer-review block,
  not a green retry; load 35–42 is an observation, not a log) carry over.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate design this work hardens.
- Sibling item: **the green-cache-entry resume path** (created alongside this one) — keeps a
  unit-stage abort from forcing a full re-run of an unchanged tree.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (bound strategy: A static raise / B load-aware only / C hybrid) — ANSWERED: C (hybrid).**
  Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment on that
  item): "1. C". Agent recommendation (adopted): C. Research: TCE `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  bounds at lines 56/92/96; `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` line 816 ("full suite takes 18–21 minutes"); measured green TCE unit stages
  from `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` — 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst
  217 s on 2026-11-11 17:37); no load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today.
- **Q2 (resume-path scope) — ANSWERED: B (split; framework item).** Answered by producer: "2. B".
  Tracked in the sibling item created alongside this one.
- **Duplicate check** — searched `wl search "hang timeout vitest retry"` (TCE) and this repo's
  items: the browser-stage precedent (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) is completed and does not cover the
  unit-stage bound, the diagnostics content, or the resume path; no duplicate found.
data.title: Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

# Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a unit-stage hang abort resumes

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release, I want a unit-stage hang abort to **not** force a full 20+ minute
re-run when the tree is unchanged: the gate should resume from a green cached full-suite entry
within the cache TTL instead of re-executing the whole suite.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The TCE v0.1.24 release gate aborted in the unit stage with a 300 s hang bound (exit 124; no
failing test — host contention, load 35–42 on 16 cores). The per-repo test cache is keyed on
command + git state with a 2 h TTL; the hang **overwrites** the cache entry for that state with
`exit_code: 124`, so a retry on the same tree re-runs every stage from scratch. The release gate
runs `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on the merged dev→main tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hang/abort result (exit `124` from the bounded vitest runner, or any non-zero abort that
  produced no parsable test results) does **not** destroy a green cache entry for the same tree
  state: when a valid green entry exists for the requested command+state within TTL, the cached
  green verdict is served even if a later aborted run wrote to the same key, and the abort is
  still reported (the gate must never *silently* accept an abort as green).
- The resume path is functional end-to-end: re-running the release gate against an unchanged tree
  (same git state, within TTL) after a unit-stage abort consumes the preserved green full-suite
  entry instead of re-executing `npm --silent test`, with the cache TTL gate intact.
- The release gate documents the resume procedure: `run_tests.py`/cache behaviour and the
  operator-visible statement ("the tree is unchanged within TTL — re-run resumes green") are
  described in this repo's release-gate docs and in `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
  comments; no green-entry destruction happens on abort.
- A failure or changed tree still executes and stores freshly — the preservation never masks a red
  run, a changed git state, or an expired TTL: cache behaviour for abort entries is covered by
  tests in this repo (`tests/` alongside `test_cache.py` / `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A contended-host abort stops costing a full re-run: the producer retries the release and the gate
resumes from the green entry for the unchanged tree, holding the green verdict while the abort is
still surfaced.

## Constraints

- **Never mask a genuine failure.** A preserved green entry is served only for the same command +
  git state within TTL; any tree change, red verdict, or TTL expiry forces a fresh run.
- **Green-first, but loud.** Returning the preserved green entry must be paired with a clear
  notice that the *aborted* run is being satisfied from the earlier green entry (operator
  visibility), not a silent acceptance of exit 124.
- **Follow the existing cache contract.** Keying, git-state fingerprinting, `scope` / `test_type`
  namespacing and the state-changed quarantine in `test_cache.py` are unchanged; this item only
  refines what a hang/abort writes.
- **Cross-repo consumers.** TCE's audit/release flows consume `query_cached()`; their
  expectations (read-only, verdicts only for matching state) must not regress.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `test_cache.py` (this repo root) — store/lookup semantics for hang/abort (exit 124) entries;
  green-entry preservation; TTL unchanged.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_cached`/`query_cached` usage, abort-result reporting.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — full-suite gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81),
  resume documentation/behaviour.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `query_cached` consumer; must still reject partial/abort
  entries as full-suite evidence.
- `tests/` — coverage for abort-vs-green preservation in this repo's test suite.
- Cross-repo (TCE, tracked here): `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout / § Test Configuration —
  document the resume path for TCE release operators.

## Related work

- **Sibling item: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit bound** (created alongside
  this one) — prevents the abort in the first place; this item makes the residual abort cheap to
  recover from. These are complementary, not sequential.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — original intake; the abort cache entry is
  `.worklog/cache/3b6572d09f1a6363f3a1be3d020af939` (TCE), `exit_code: 124`, facts
  `elapsed=311.09s, configured_timeout=1500s`.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate that the release gate
  mirrors (cached runner makes repeat verification cheap).
- **WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3** and `test_cache.py` pre-run/post-run keying history — the cache-state
  semantics this item must preserve.
- TCE CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N (browser-stage hang bound) and CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H (coverage gate) —
  the fail-closed invariants that must not regress.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q2 (resume-path scope: A docs only / B split into a framework item / C in-item framework
  edit) — ANSWERED: B (framework item; this item is that split).** Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in
  intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment): "2. B". Agent recommendation
  (adopted): the cache and gate are framework-owned here (`test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), so the
  implementation lands in this repo and every project's release gate benefits from the fix;
  TCE-side documentation is cross-repo work recorded on this item.
- **Q1 (bound strategy) — ANSWERED separately** (C, hybrid): tracked in the sibling item; the
  diagnostic content it adds is what makes the abort entry's context readable here.
- **Duplicate check** — no existing item preserves green cache entries across abort results;
  `test_cache.py` writes the returned verdict unconditionally on the post-run state today (TCE
  `run_cached` usage observed via the 124 entry at 3b6572d09f…).

# `implement.py start` must not fork a worktree from a local parent branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`

Mirror of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MWFF40700014EE2** (`discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`).
Per the precedent producer decision for **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 ← AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(2026-09-25: "the fix and regression tests live in the SorraAgents counterpart; no
implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix lives here, where
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is.

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`, but
`_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is diverged or cannot
be fetched non-checked-out (`reason: "diverged_or_checked_out"`), and `phase_start` then
forks the worktree from that stale local `dev` anyway (`git_worktree_add(branch,
abs_wt_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <wt> dev`). The child
session inherits a base missing commits already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev` (`e38797b8` local-only,
  duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an unrelated
  `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against pre-fix source and went **red** on a failure
  `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS` still listing the deleted
  `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (`8d1c1aca`) by hand before it could pass its
  gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push to dev
initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and retried"), so this is
recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref whose commits are all contained in
`origin/<parent>` (a fast-forward ancestor of `origin/<parent>`), so a driven child never
starts behind the published base.

## Approach (decided)

The AI_Hell report listed two candidate approaches ("fork from `origin/<parent>`" or
"warn loudly"); the acceptance criteria pin the first and make the second mandatory
reporting, so both are in scope:

1. `_sync_parent_branch` reports `ahead`/`behind` counts (via
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) on every
   skip reason where the counts are computable, in addition to `reason`/`warning`.
2. A new resolver decides the fork base: **fork from
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` whenever the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, which includes the diverged case); otherwise keep the current local-branch
   base.** The local ref is never force-updated — a diverged local `dev` stays exactly as it
   is for the operator to reconcile.
3. `phase_start` records the choice: `report["steps"]["worktree_base"] = {ref, reason,
   ahead, behind}` and an extended "Implementation started"/"resumed" comment naming the base
   ref and, when the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
4. Fail-open is preserved: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch, or a dirty main checkout
   never blocks `start`; when the counts cannot be computed (fetch failed / no remote-tracking
   ref) the local branch remains the base exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded or the worktree is forked
  from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent branch
  was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first changed-scope
  gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh still fails
  open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch.

## Implementation sketch

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): add `ahead`/`behind` to the skipped results
    (`diverged`, `diverged_or_checked_out`, and the other safe-skip paths where computable).
  - New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
    returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`; picks
    `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when behind > 0.
  - `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): pass the resolved ref to `git_worktree_add`, record
    `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, and name it in the start/resume comment (~line 11431).
  - `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): document that the base may be a fully-qualified
    remote-tracking ref; assert the new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` (the
    `--track` upstream must not change — `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`).
- Tests (test-first, new file `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, following
  the hermetic-fixture patterns in `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` /
  `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (start section ~2204-2216, ~4029) and
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~357) — document the base-ref resolution and the new report
  keys/skip reasons.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2` (AI_Hell discovery report; counterpart of this item)
- SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 (completed) — `finish` now fast-forwards local `dev` after the push;
  that closes the *common* stale-local-dev case, leaving the diverged/lock-held skip this
  item fixes.
- SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO — main-checkout lock shared by `start`'s refresh and `finish`.
- SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF — `start` resume-from-worktree path resolved against the main checkout.
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree detection (same "stale base" family).

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a rebase and a red
gate on work someone else already shipped.
data.title: implement.py start forks a driven worktree from a diverged local dev

# Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1). This is the single biggest time sink identified in the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` acquires the per-repository `flock`
(`<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`) at Step 3c and holds it until
the `finally` block — covering commit → fast-forward local dev → **push** → post-push
verification. The dev push triggers `.githooks/pre-push`, which runs the **full test
suite** (`run_tests.py --scope full`, measured ~326 s / 5.4 min for AI_Hell) while the
lock is held. A read-only test run is therefore made part of the exclusive mutating
critical section, so every concurrent `finish` serialises its ~5-min suite behind the
others. This is the root cause of the 37% `wait_for_job` share and the 46 lock-waits
(median 5 min, max 21.5 min).

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions.
- **Implement-skill session** whose `finish` currently spends most of its wall-clock
  waiting for the lock rather than doing work.

User stories:

- As an operator running a 6-way fan-out, I want concurrent finishes to overlap their
  full-suite gate runs so the batch finishes in roughly the time of one work item
  rather than the sum of all of them.
- As an implement-skill session, I want the exclusive repository lock to cover only
  the short mutating window, so my `finish` is not blocked for another session's
  ~5-minute test run.

## Goal

As an operator running concurrent implement sessions, I want the full-suite gate to
run **without** holding the exclusive repository lock, so concurrent finishes overlap
their test time instead of queueing on it.

## Approach

- Resolve the full-suite verdict for the *pushed tree* **before** taking the
  main-checkout lock (the tree-keyed cache already exists — reuse it), or run the
  suite under only the shared `test` semaphore lane, not the repo lock.
- Keep the lock covering only the true mutations: commit → fast-forward → push →
  ancestry assertion (should be seconds).
- Preserve the existing safety invariants: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev`
  ref, the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and the tree/provenance binding of
  the verdict (no verdict about a different tree may be trusted).

## Acceptance criteria

- The full test suite is never executed while `main-checkout.lock` is held (asserted
  by a test that observes lock state across the suite invocation).
- The lock-hold window in a green `finish` is bounded and does not include the
  full-suite duration (measured/asserted in a test or documented metric).
- A concurrent-finish integration test shows the second finish's wait is materially
  shorter when the first is running the full suite (no longer serialised on suite
  time).
- No regression in the existing finish-concurrency / ancestry-assertion tests.
- At least one automated test proves the new gate/lock ordering (lock state observed
  while the suite runs, and a green finish whose lock window excludes the suite).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The shared `dev` ref stays single-owner: exactly one finish mutates it at a time and
  the ancestry assertion after the push is unchanged.
- The gate verdict remains provenance-bound and tree-keyed (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV,
  SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB): no verdict about a different tree may be reused, and a
  rebased commit legitimately produces a new tree (see the sibling rebase item).
- The bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` behaviour is preserved — no unbounded
  lock hold.
- Out of scope: trimming the full suite's own runtime, sharding, per-file caching,
  raising `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (per-project concerns), and changing changed-scope
  test selection.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` acquires `main-checkout.lock` at Step 3c and holds it through push
  and post-push verification.
- `.githooks/pre-push` always runs `run_tests.py --scope full` for pushes to
  `dev`/`main` (scope-aware gate, SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61) and is bound to the pushed
  commit (`--gate-commit`), with a tree-keyed verdict cache and cache mirroring into
  the main checkout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` already allocates an independent `test` semaphore
  lane and caches verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.

## Desired change

The expensive read-only suite runs outside the exclusive repository lock (either
before acquiring it, keyed on the would-be pushed tree, or under the `test` lane
only), and the lock window shrinks to the commit → fast-forward → push → ancestry
assertion sequence.

## Impact

Concurrent finishes stop serialising behind each other's full-suite runs, so an
operator's 6-way fan-out batch completes in roughly the time of a single work item
instead of queueing six ~5-minute suites one after another.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock acquisition and the push/gate window (search `Step 3c`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate entry point, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate that today runs inside the lock window
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / `release_repo_lock` implementing `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — existing lock-window tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish lock/timeout documentation to update

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — lock helper reused here.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — establishes the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite is at the gate at all.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item must reuse.
- Sibling items: Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC).
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — feeds the epic-level before/after measurement.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making the suite asynchronous (background gate) would weaken
  the "never push an unverified tree" guarantee — out of scope; the verdict must still
  gate the push.
- **Risk:** moving the suite before the lock could test a tree that is then invalidated
  by a rebase; mitigations: reuse the tree-keyed verdict, and treat a rebase-produced
  tree as a cache miss (handled by the sibling rebase item).
- **Assumption:** the `dev` push gate stays `scope=full` for release-critical refs.
- **Assumption:** the suite's own runtime is a per-project concern; only the serialising
  effect is addressed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session analysis recorded on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), plus operator decisions recorded
there (concurrency target up to 6; per-project full-suite trimming out of scope).
Researched directly in the repository: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
(Step 3c lock window), `.githooks/pre-push` (full-suite gate), and
`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (tree-keyed verdict cache).
